alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity from ERP: field 'ShipDate' must be ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), got '21/11/2026'

arguments.query: HTTP 422 field must be ISO-8601 date format wrong value fix and resend
ShipDate not ISO-8601 date format 422 ERP order

arguments.reason: ERP rejected the order with HTTP 422 because ShipDate '21/11/2026' is not ISO-8601. Since 21 cannot be a month, the value is unambiguously 21 November 2026, so the corrected field is ShipDate=2026-11-21; per runbook 04-data-validation a date reorder is a correction and needs operator approval. First attempt, no earlier failures or similar incidents on Demo.ERP.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Add an ISO-8601 date conversion to the source mapping/DTL for OrderRequest.ShipDate (DD/MM/YYYY -> YYYY-MM-DD) so the ERP no longer receives non-ISO dates; other fields already comply with the data quality policy.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity from ERP: unsupported currency 'EURO' (supported: EUR,USD,GBP,CHF)

arguments.query: unsupported currency validation error mapping currency name to ISO code
unsupported currency EURO EUR 422

arguments.reason: ERP rejected 'EURO' with HTTP 422 (unsupported currency; supported: EUR,USD,GBP,CHF). Per runbook 04-data-validation, a currency name to its ISO 4217 code is a pure normalization of form, so patch Currency to 'EUR' and resend. No earlier attempts failed and no similar failures in the last 7 days.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Add currency name → ISO 4217 code conversion to the source mapping/DTL for Triage.Demo.OrderRequest so 'EURO'-style values never reach Demo.ERP.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 409 Conflict from ERP: order SO-1001 already exists (created 2026-10-21 22:26:33) with identical content

arguments.query: HTTP 409 Conflict duplicate message already exists discard
HTTP 409 Conflict order already exists identical content duplicate

arguments.reason: ERP returned HTTP 409 stating order SO-1001 already exists with identical content, so this is an exact duplicate (runbook 06-duplicates: exact duplicates must not be processed again). First attempt for this message, no prior failures, and no similar failures on Demo.ERP in the last week.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Make the duplicate case a non-error: add a ReplyCodeActions rule on Demo.ERP treating "HTTP 409 ... identical content" as success (or have the source/target use an idempotency key / upsert), so source resubmissions stop raising alerts.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 401 Unauthorized from ERP: API token for tenant C-0042 expired on 2026-10-01

arguments.query: HTTP 401 Unauthorized expired API token credentials
ERP HTTP 401 expired API token credentials

arguments.reason: HTTP 401 with "API token for tenant C-0042 expired on 2026-10-01" is a deterministic credential failure: runbook 03-authentication.md forbids retrying unchanged or altering the message, and only a person can rotate the token. No earlier attempts of this message and no similar failures in the last 24h, so the message itself is valid and must be held for the operator.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Rotate the ERP API token for tenant C-0042 and update the Demo.ERP Credentials setting (IRIS Credentials/Wallet); track token expiry with an alert well before expiry, and alert on authentication errors separately from data errors so the FailureTimeout retries (5s interval / 15s timeout) are not wasted on deterministic 401s (consider ReplyCodeActions for 401 = no retry).

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 409 Conflict from ERP: business rule BR-12 violated, order amount must be positive (got -120)

arguments.query: business rule violation negative amount order rejected
HTTP 409 Conflict business rule violated negative order amount

arguments.reason: ERP returned HTTP 409 with business rule BR-12 violated (order amount must be positive, got -120) for SO-1006. Runbook 05-business-rules.md states retrying is pointless and amounts must never be altered to satisfy a rule; only the business can say whether the negative amount reflects a genuine credit/return or a source error. First attempt, no similar failures in the last 24h.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Validate BR-12 (positive order amount) earlier in the flow — in the business process or a DTL — and route rejected orders to a work queue instead of failing at the ERP operation; check the source mapping that produced Amount=-120 for SO-1006.

alertText: ERROR <Ens>ErrFailureTimeout: FailureTimeout of 15 seconds exceeded in Triage.Demo.ERPOperation; status from last attempt was ERROR #5001: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway from ERP: ERP application server unavailable (upstream connect error)

arguments.query: HTTP 502 Bad Gateway upstream connect error FailureTimeout exceeded retry
HTTP 502 Bad Gateway upstream connect error ERP application server unavailable FailureTimeout exceeded
FailureTimeout exceeded business operation decision guidance retry grace period

arguments.reason: First attempt of this message (no earlier failures, no similar failures in 72h). The FailureTimeout of 15s was exhausted while the ERP target returned HTTP 502 "application server unavailable" — a transient server-side outage per runbook 08-rate-limits-and-server-errors; the message payload is valid, so resend unchanged after 60s.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: FailureTimeout (15s) with RetryInterval 5s is too short for a 502 outage — it converts ordinary target blips into failed messages (runbook 02). Raise FailureTimeout to a few minutes and/or set ReplyCodeActions so HTTP 5xx/connection errors are retried natively instead of failing the message; coordinate capacity/maintenance windows with the ERP owner.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity from ERP: field 'ShipDate' must be ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD), got '28/11/2026'

arguments.query: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity date format ISO-8601 ship date validation
ShipDate must be ISO-8601 date format 422 ERP order

arguments.reason: ERP rejected ShipDate '28/11/2026' for not being ISO-8601 (HTTP 422). Incident 1 is the identical failure for the same customer C-0019 (ShipDate '21/11/2026'); the operator note there records that sales confirmed customer C-0019 always sends dates as DD/MM/YYYY, and the DTL fix is tracked in INT-4411. Applying that documented convention, 28/11/2026 is 2026-11-28; per runbook 04-data-validation a date reorder is a correction, so this needs operator approval.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Add a DD/MM/YYYY→YYYY-MM-DD conversion for ShipDate in the source DTL/mapping (already requested in ticket INT-4411) so orders of customer C-0019 stop failing at the ERP; consider a ReplyCodeActions rule so HTTP 422 validation errors alert immediately instead of being retried.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 401 Unauthorized from ERP: API token for tenant C-0042 expired on 2026-10-01

arguments.query: HTTP 401 Unauthorized expired API token ERP tenant

arguments.reason: HTTP 401 "API token for tenant C-0042 expired on 2026-10-01" is a deterministic credential failure: runbook 03-authentication.md forbids retrying unchanged or altering the message, and only a person can rotate the token (the component's RetryInterval=5/FailureTimeout=15 retries cannot fix it). Same failure and tenant was handled as incident 4, where the operator renewed credential ERP-C0042 and resent the order; this message (SO-1105) is valid and must be held for that token renewal.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Store the ERP tenant token in IRIS Credentials/Wallet and track its expiry — tenant C-0042 tokens expire yearly on Oct 1 — with a proactive rotation reminder and a separate alert for authentication errors so expired credentials are caught before orders fail.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 404 Not Found from WMS: SKU 'SKU-999' is not in the item master

arguments.query: SKU not in item master, HTTP 404 from WMS target, unknown item
SKU not in item master HTTP 404 WMS unknown SKU stock update
data validation business rule violation unknown reference value not found in master data, cannot correct

arguments.reason: WMS rejects the message with ERROR #5001 HTTP 404 "SKU 'SKU-999' is not in the item master" — a master-data/business-rule rejection of the reference value, not a transient fault. The correct SKU cannot be derived from the payload ({Sku: SKU-999, Warehouse: MIL01, Quantity: 3, Unit: EA}), so retrying or patching would be a guess; no prior attempts, no similar past incidents and no recurring pattern on Demo.WMS (0 failures in 7 days) give no reusable guidance.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: Have the business confirm whether SKU-999 should exist in the WMS item master (create it there) or whether the source sent an invalid/wrong SKU. Add an item-master lookup/validation in the source mapping or DTL so unknown SKUs are caught before reaching Demo.WMS, and consider a ReplyCodeActions rule for HTTP 404 so such business rejections are routed to a person instead of being auto-retried.

alertText: ERROR #5001: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable from WMS: scheduled maintenance in progress. Retry-After: 30

arguments.query: HTTP 503 service unavailable scheduled maintenance Retry-After
Demo.WMS HTTP 503 scheduled maintenance Retry-After resend stock update

arguments.reason: HTTP 503 with "scheduled maintenance in progress" is transient; runbook 08-rate-limits-and-server-errors says 429/503 should be resent later respecting the target's Retry-After, which is 30 seconds. This is the first attempt of the message, no earlier attempts exist, the payload is valid, and Demo.WMS has no other failures in the last 24h, so a delayed out-of-band resend after 30s is the right handling.
arguments.upstreamRecommendation: The WMS target has planned maintenance windows; consider raising queueing tolerance on Demo.WMS (e.g. FailureTimeout -1 with alerting on queue size, per runbook 02) so planned outages do not surface as failed messages.
